title: 10,000km Later: Was My Chinese Superbike Worth It?

takeaways.text: The large (about 56 cm) matched a Tarmac's stack and reach for him at 181 cm; the frameset comes with a chosen bar width and stem length, a sturdy computer mount and aero bottles.
SEKA sells framesets only, through one UK shop; the builder found clean bottom-bracket threads, steerer surfaces and good tolerances.
Over about 10,000 km it was trouble-free and needed no warranty claims.

He rates it as quick as a Madone, Aeroad or Tarmac (behind a BMC Teammachine R), with excellent cornering, but the stiff front end remains the one comfort weakness against a compliant seatpost and rear.

disclosure: How the frame was obtained is not stated; this is the same Ultegra Di2 Spear as his first review, professionally built by a UK shop.
summary: A 17-month, roughly 10,000 km follow-up on the reviewer's SEKA Spear.
